claim.title: Underparameterized risk approximation (Claim 2)
claim.statement: Let gamma=n/d>1. For the ordinary-least-squares estimator, the bias is B_n=0 and the variance is approximately V_n ~ sigma^2/(gamma-1).
claim.test_plan: Fix d=1000, ||beta||_2=1, sigma=0.1. For gamma>1 (e.g., n=ceil(gamma*d) with gamma up to 5), generate many independent training sets. Compute the OLS estimator beta_hat=(X^T X)^{-1} X^T y. Estimate bias B_n=||beta-E[beta_hat]||^2 and variance V_n=E[||beta_hat-E[beta_hat]||^2] by Monte Carlo. Compare to 0 and sigma^2/(gamma-1).
claim.success_criterion: The empirical bias is numerically zero (e.g., relative to ||beta||^2 it is <0.01), and the empirical variance agrees with sigma^2/(gamma-1) within 20% relative error for gamma in [1.05,5].
